title: Recall Quiz: Restoration Age & John Dryden

questions.q: The Restoration period in English literature begins in the year 1660, which marks:
options: The publication of Shakespeare's First Folio
The beginning of the English Civil War
The return of the monarchy under King Charles II
The signing of the Magna Carta
questions.explanation: The monarchy was restored in 1660 after the Puritan Commonwealth.

questions.q: Who was appointed as England's first official Poet Laureate in 1668?
questions.explanation: While Ben Jonson was the unofficial first, John Dryden received the first official royal patent.

questions.q: Dryden's 'Mac Flecknoe' is a mock-heroic satire attacking which rival poet?
questions.explanation: Dryden relentlessly mocks Thomas Shadwell, crowning him the ruler of the realm of Nonsense.

questions.q: Which of Dryden's plays is an adaptation of Shakespeare's 'Antony and Cleopatra'?
questions.explanation: All for Love is Dryden's version, written to conform to classical dramatic unities.

questions.q: The 'Comedy of Manners', popular during the Restoration, primarily satirized:
options: The affectations of the upper-class society
questions.explanation: These plays focused on the witty, often immoral behavior of high society.

questions.q: Which play is considered the masterpiece of the Restoration Comedy of Manners?
questions.explanation: William Congreve's 'The Way of the World' (1700) is the pinnacle of the genre.

questions.q: Who is recognized as the first English woman to earn her living as a professional writer?
questions.explanation: Aphra Behn broke barriers for female writers in the 17th century.

questions.q: John Dryden perfected which poetic form, heavily using it for his satires?
questions.explanation: Dryden mastered the Heroic Couplet (rhyming pairs of iambic pentameter).
